theory: State the real-domain conditions for the conversion laws: root indices are integers at least 2, even roots require nonnegative radicands, and denominator roots must be nonzero. The unrestricted rooting/powering equivalence and the claim that a divisible power always simplifies directly to the integer index are false for negative bases with even roots; in particular, $\sqrt[4]{y^{12}}=|y|^3$, not universally $y^3$, so explicitly establish the nonnegative-variable convention or qualify these laws.
